problems.title: Separate odd and even geometric terms
problems.question: A geometric progression has an even number of terms. The ratio of the sum of all terms to the sum of the even-position terms is 1.5. Find its ratio q.
problems.idea: Each even-position term is q times the preceding odd-position term.
formulas: If O is the odd-position sum, the even-position sum is E=qO.
steps: The total sum is O+E. Thus (O+E)/E=1+O/E=1+1/q.
Set 1+1/q=1.5. Then 1/q=0.5 and q=2.

problems.title: Area from centroid-to-vertex distances
problems.question: Triangle ABC has centroid M and distances MA=5, MB=8, MC=7. Find its area.
problems.idea: The three centroid vectors sum to zero. This finds the angle between MA and MB, then the area of triangle AMB.
formulas: Triangle area $=ab\sin\theta/2$; the centroid divides a triangle into three equal-area vertex-pair triangles.
steps: Because MA+MB=-MC, its squared length is 49. Hence 49=25+64+80cosθ, giving cosθ=-1/2.
The full triangle has three times that area.

problems.title: Midpoint of two graph intersections
problems.question: The graphs $y=x^2+4x-6$ and $y=2x+2$ meet at A,B. Find the midpoint of AB.
problems.idea: Equate the two expressions for y, then find both points.
formulas: At an intersection both graph equations hold.
Midpoint coordinates are the averages of endpoint coordinates.
steps: The intersections have x=-4,2 and, from the line, y=-6,6.

problems.title: Recover a number removed from an average
problems.question: The numbers 1 through 20 were written down. One is erased, and the mean of the remaining numbers is 11. Which number was erased?
problems.idea: Compare the total before and after removing one number.
steps: The original total is 20·21/2=210.
After the erasure, 19 numbers total 19·11=209.
The missing number is 210-209=1.

problems.title: Annulus between an equilateral triangle’s two circles
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has side 6 cm. Find the area between its circumcircle and incircle.
problems.idea: Both radii follow from the triangle’s altitude.
formulas: Equilateral height h=s√3/2; circumradius R=2h/3 and inradius r=h/3.
steps: The height is 3√3, so R=2√3 and r=√3.
The squared-radius difference is 12-3=9.
The annulus area is 9π square centimetres.

problems.title: A composite-function inequality with a missing input
problems.question: Solve f(g(x))≤1 for $f(t)=(3t+7)/(4t+6)$ and $g(x)=2/(x-3)$.
problems.idea: Find the composite’s original domain before simplifying.
formulas: Rational inequalities are solved by testing signs around numerator zeros and denominator poles.
steps: The second domain restriction gives 8/(x-3)+6≠0, so x≠5/3.
On that domain, f(g(x))=(7x-15)/(6x-10). Subtracting 1 gives (x-5)/(6x-10)≤0.
This ratio is nonpositive between its pole 5/3 and zero 5, including 5 but excluding the pole.
Also remove x=3, where g itself is undefined.
problems.note: The highlighted choice (5/3,5] overlooks x=3. A simplification of the composite does not restore an input excluded by the inner function.

problems.title: Symmetric expressions in two quadratic roots
problems.question: The roots x1,x2 of $x^2+x-1=0$ are used in $\frac{x_1^3-x_2^3}{1/x_1^2-1/x_2^2}$. Find its value.
problems.idea: Factor out their difference, then use the root sum and product.
steps: The numerator is (x1-x2)[(-1)²-(-1)]=2(x1-x2).
The denominator is (x2²-x1²)/(x1x2)²=-(x1-x2)(x1+x2)=x1-x2.
The roots are distinct and nonzero because the discriminant is 5 and product is -1. Cancel their nonzero difference.

problems.title: Sides, diagonals and symmetry axes
problems.question: A regular polygon has 18 more diagonals than sides. Find its number of symmetry axes.
problems.idea: First determine its number of sides, then use regular-polygon symmetry.
formulas: A regular n-gon has n symmetry axes.
steps: Set n(n-3)/2=n+18. This gives n²-5n-36=0.
Factor as (n-9)(n+4)=0. The valid side count is n=9.
A regular nonagon therefore has 9 symmetry axes.

problems.title: Union of independent events
problems.question: Independent events A,B have probabilities 0.4 and 0.7. Find P(A∪B).
problems.idea: Subtract the overlap once from the sum of the individual probabilities.
steps: The intersection probability is 0.4·0.7=0.28.
The union probability is 0.4+0.7-0.28=0.82.

problems.title: A radical reciprocal and a cube identity
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt x+\sqrt2)^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt x-\sqrt2}{x\sqrt x-\sqrt8}\right)^{-1}$.
problems.idea: Use the difference-of-cubes factorisation for the reciprocal term.
formulas: Let t=√x and r=√2, so x√x=t³ and √8=r³.
steps: The original expression requires x≥0 and x≠2. At x=2 the fraction is undefined.
The reciprocal fraction becomes (t³-r³)/(t-r)=t²+tr+r².
The first square is t²+2tr+r². Subtracting leaves tr=√(2x).

problems.title: Sum a linear function at forty inputs
problems.question: For f(x)=3x-2, find f(1)+f(2)+...+f(40).
problems.idea: Sum the linear terms and the constant terms separately.
steps: The input sum is 40·41/2=820.
The required sum is 3·820-2·40=2460-80=2380.

problems.title: Integer values in a finite rational sequence
problems.question: For n=1,...,50, how many terms of $a_n=(7n-36)/(n+7)$ are integers?
problems.idea: Divide the numerator by the denominator to turn the condition into a divisibility question.
steps: The term is an integer exactly when n+7 divides 85.
The possible denominators run from 8 to 57. The positive divisors of 85 are 1,5,17,85.
Only 17 is in that interval. It corresponds to n=10 and a10=2.
Therefore exactly one term is an integer.
problems.note: The printed choices begin at 2 and the highlighted choice is 2. They do not match the stated formula and index range; the divisor check gives one term.

problems.title: Two ordered draws without replacement
problems.question: The listed balls are labelled i,a,i,g,b. Two are drawn in order without replacement. What is the probability of drawing the word ia?
problems.idea: Count the two i balls for the first draw and the single a ball for the second.
formulas: P(first i then a)=P(first i)·P(second a given first i).
steps: The list contains five balls, including two labelled i.
The probability of i first is 2/5. After drawing it, the probability of a is 1/4.
problems.answer: 1/10 (option ვ), using the five listed balls.
problems.note: The sentence says “four balls” but lists five labels. The answer uses the explicit list, which is also consistent with the highlighted choice.

problems.title: Arc length with an angle in radians
problems.question: Find an arc length when the radius is 8 cm and the central angle is 3π/4 radians.
problems.idea: A radian angle directly multiplies the radius.
formulas: Arc length L=rθ when θ is in radians.
steps: Substitute r=8 and θ=3π/4.

problems.title: A diagonal splits part of a trapezoid
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has bases BC=b and AD=2b. A parallel section EF cuts the legs in ratio 1:3 measured from the smaller base. The original diagonal AC meets EF at K. Find the area ratio of the two pieces it cuts from trapezoid AEFD.
problems.idea: Find the section length and the small triangle AEK by similarity, then subtract its area from the lower trapezoid.
formulas: Parallel section lengths interpolate linearly with height.
Similar triangles have squared area ratios.
Trapezoid area is average base times height.
steps: Let the full height be H. Section EF lies H/4 below BC, so its length is b+(2b-b)/4=5b/4. The lower trapezoid has height 3H/4.
Triangle AEK is similar to ABC with scale 3/4. Since [ABC]=bH/2, its area is (9/16)(bH/2)=9bH/32.
The other piece has area (39-9)bH/32=30bH/32. Thus the ratio is 9:30=3:10.
problems.answer: 3:10 (option ვ), smaller piece to larger piece.

problems.title: A 5–12–13 triangle from a decimal leg ratio
problems.question: The ratio of a right triangle’s legs is 2.4. Its circumradius exceeds its inradius by 9 dm. Find its area.
problems.idea: The leg ratio is 12:5, so scale a 5–12–13 triangle.
steps: The circumradius is 13t/2 and inradius is (5t+12t-13t)/2=2t.
The difference is 9t/2=9, giving t=2.
The legs are 10 and 24 dm, so the area is 10·24/2=120 dm².

problems.title: Side count from a regular polygon angle
problems.question: A regular polygon has interior angle 160°. How many sides does it have?
problems.idea: Use the exterior angle, whose full-turn sum is 360 degrees.
formulas: For a regular n-gon, exterior angle=360°/n.
steps: The exterior angle is 20°.

problems.title: When two vectors enclose an acute angle
problems.question: For which k do vectors (-3,k) and (0,-1) enclose an acute angle?
problems.idea: A positive dot product means a positive cosine, hence an acute angle.
formulas: u·v=|u||v|cosθ; the vector lengths here are nonzero.
steps: The dot product is (-3)·0+k(-1)=-k.
Require -k>0, giving k<0. Equality would give a right angle.

problems.title: Octagon area from a dodecagon in one circle
problems.question: A regular dodecagon inscribed in a circle has area 18√2 cm². Find the area of a regular octagon inscribed in the same circle.
problems.idea: Both areas can be expressed using the common circumradius.
steps: The dodecagon area is 6R²sin30°=3R², giving R²=6√2.
The octagon area is 4R²sin45°=2√2R².
Substitute to obtain 2√2·6√2=24 cm².

problems.title: Probability from an inscribed triangle’s area
problems.question: A point is chosen uniformly in the circumdisk of an equilateral triangle. What is the probability that it lies inside the triangle?
problems.idea: For a uniform point, probability is the favourable area divided by the whole disk area.
formulas: An equilateral triangle of circumradius R has area 3√3R²/4.
steps: Divide 3√3R²/4 by πR².
The radius cancels, leaving 3√3/(4π).

problems.title: Reflect the origin across a line
problems.question: Find the reflection of the origin in line 3x+4y=12.
problems.idea: The perpendicular from the origin has direction equal to the line’s normal vector (3,4). Double the foot to obtain the reflected point.
formulas: The foot on Ax+By=C from the origin is H=C(A,B)/(A²+B²).
Reflection point P=2H when the original point is the origin.
steps: The midpoint OP lies on the line, and OP is parallel to its normal, confirming the reflection.

problems.title: Separate a barrel’s mass from its contents
problems.question: A barrel full of milk weighs 400 kg. After one-third of the milk is removed, it weighs 290 kg. Find the empty barrel’s mass.
problems.idea: The decrease in total mass is exactly the milk removed.
steps: The removed milk weighs 400-290=110 kg.
That is one-third of the original milk, so the milk initially weighs 330 kg.
The barrel weighs 400-330=70 kg.

problems.title: Axis-intercept triangle under an absolute-value graph
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle formed by the axis intercepts of $y=-|x^2-5x+6|+3$.
problems.idea: Find all x-intercepts by considering both signs of the inner polynomial, then use the y-intercept as the height.
steps: The positive branch gives x²-5x+3=0, with roots (5±√13)/2.
The negative branch gives x²-5x+9=0, whose discriminant is -11, so there are no further real intercepts.
The x-intercepts are √13 units apart. At x=0 the graph has y=-6+3=-3, so the perpendicular height is 3.
The triangle area is 3√13/2.

problems.title: Count only positive polynomial roots
problems.question: How many positive roots does 3x³-4x²-4x=0 have?
problems.idea: Factor out x and then factor the quadratic.
steps: The roots are 0,-2/3,2.
Only 2 is positive; zero does not count as positive.

problems.title: Disjoint events with inconsistent marginal probabilities
problems.question: Events A,B are said to be disjoint, with P(A)=0.4 and P(B)=0.7. What is P(A∩B), and are these data consistent?
problems.idea: Disjointness forces an empty intersection, but the total probability must also stay at most one.
formulas: Disjoint events satisfy P(A∩B)=0 and P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B).
steps: The formal consequence of disjointness is P(A∩B)=0, the listed option ვ.
However, their union would then have probability 0.4+0.7=1.1, which is impossible.
Therefore no probability model satisfies all the stated assumptions simultaneously.
problems.answer: The intended intersection answer is 0 (option ვ), but the full data are inconsistent.
problems.note: This differs from the independent-events question earlier in the quiz. A disjoint pair cannot have marginal probabilities summing to more than one.
